record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For semantic subtyping enriched with polymorphic types, especially in the presence of contravariant type constructors such as arrow types and write-channel types, can one design a practical and semantically well-motivated polymorphism discipline? More specifically, can the marking approach to polymorphism be extended to contravariant constructors, can some of the original substitution-based polymorphic subtyping be recovered, and can one impose useful programming-language restrictions on polymorphic functions that keep the language both expressive and tractable?

evidence.quote: However, it is still matter of research how to implement the marking approach in the presence of contravariant type constructors: first and foremost in the presence of arrow types, as this would yield the definition of a polymorphic version of Duce; but also, it would be interesting to study the marking approach in the presence of the contravariant ch− type constructor, to check how it combines with the checks of atomicity required by the mix with the ch+ constructor, and see whether markings could suggests a solution to avoid this check of atomicity.

Finally, one can explore a more programming language oriented approach and check whether it is possible to define reasonable restrictions on the definition of polymorphic functions ... so that the resulting language provides the programmer with sufficient polymorphism for practical usage, while keeping it simple and manageable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In semantic subtyping, types are interpreted as subsets of a model of values, and the subtyping relation t ≤ s is defined to hold when the interpretation of t is contained in that of s. Standard type constructors include products, unions, intersections, negations, arrow types t → s (contravariant in the domain, covariant in the codomain), and channel types: a covariant read-channel constructor ch+(t) and a contravariant write-channel constructor ch−(t).

A polymorphic extension introduces type variables α, β, …. One known technique, the "marking approach", interprets each type variable as a tag/marking placed on subparts of values, so that polymorphic subtyping is reduced to a containment property on marked sets of values. So far, the marking approach has been worked out only for purely covariant constructors (e.g. products, ch+).

Problem. Provide all of the following, or prove that no such constructions can satisfy the stated requirements:

(a) Extend the marking approach to a setting that includes the contravariant arrow constructor →, yielding a decidable polymorphic subtyping relation that is sound and complete with respect to a set-theoretic model of values, and that supports a type-checking algorithm for a polymorphic functional calculus with arrow types, unions, intersections, and negations.

(b) Extend the marking approach in the presence of both ch+ and ch− channel constructors, analyse how markings interact with the atomicity side-conditions required when ch+ and ch− are combined, and determine whether markings allow one to drop or weaken those atomicity checks.

(c) Identify a fragment of the marking-based polymorphic subtyping relation that coincides with a substitution-based notion of polymorphism — i.e. where t ≤ s holds polymorphically iff every type-substitution instance σ(t) ≤ σ(s) holds monomorphically — and characterize this fragment precisely.

(d) Formulate syntactic restrictions on the definition of polymorphic functions in such a calculus (e.g. on how type variables may occur in domains and codomains of arrows) that yield a language which is (i) expressive enough for typical programming uses of parametric polymorphism, (ii) has decidable type checking with tractable complexity, and (iii) admits a sound and complete typing algorithm relative to the semantic model.
artifact.status_search_result: A marking-based polymorphic semantic subtyping has been developed for covariant constructors (products, ch+), and a separate convexity/substitution-based theory of polymorphism exists for arrow types (Castagna et al., ICFP 2011; LMCS 2020). However, no published work appears to extend the marking approach itself to contravariant constructors (arrows, ch−), nor to give the requested practical polymorphism discipline for a polymorphic CDuce. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Set-theoretic Foundation of Parametric Polymorphism and Subtyping
status_evidence.snippet: Polymorphic semantic subtyping built on a 'convexity' / substitution-based interpretation of type variables for arrow types.
status_evidence.claim: Substitution-based polymorphism for arrow types is studied, but the marking approach is not extended to contravariant constructors.

status_evidence.title: Covariance and Contravariance: a fresh look at an old issue (LMCS 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of covariance/contravariance in semantic subtyping with polymorphism.
status_evidence.claim: The handling of contravariant constructors in semantically motivated polymorphism remains an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: CDuce papers and talks
status_evidence.snippet: List of papers on the CDuce language and semantic subtyping.
status_evidence.claim: No published implementation of a fully polymorphic CDuce based on the marking approach is listed.
